breakfast.name: Gaufre de Liège (Liège Waffle)
instructions: Dissolve yeast in warm milk
Mix flour, eggs, salt, vanilla; add yeast mixture
Knead, then incorporate softened butter gradually — dough should be sticky and rich
Rise 1 hour
Fold in pearl sugar — do not dissolve it, the chunks are essential
Divide into balls, rise 15 more min
Press each into hot waffle iron
Cook until caramelized and golden — the pearl sugar melts into crunchy pockets
Eat plain, by hand, still warm
breakfast.description: The real Belgian waffle — dense, buttery, with pockets of caramelized pearl sugar. Nothing like the fluffy rectangular 'Belgian waffles' abroad.

breakfast.name: Pistolet with Cheese and Charcuterie
instructions: Split pistolets
Butter generously
Fill with cheese and charcuterie
Add a spread of sirop de Liège for the sweet-savory combination
breakfast.description: The Belgian Sunday breakfast — crusty pistolet rolls with aged cheese and cured meats. Sirop de Liège (apple-pear spread) on the side is essential.

breakfast.name: Cramique (Raisin Bread)
instructions: Mix dough with flour, yeast, sugar, eggs, milk, salt
Knead in butter until smooth and elastic
Fold in raisins
Rise 1 hour
Shape into loaves
Top with pearl sugar
Bake at 180°C for 30-35 min
breakfast.description: Sweet raisin bread topped with crunchy pearl sugar — sliced thick and eaten with butter for breakfast.

lunch.name: Moules-Frites (Mussels and Fries)
ingredients: Frites: 1.5kg Bintje potatoes, beef tallow or oil
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick batons (1cm+), rinse, soak in cold water 30 min
Dry thoroughly — water is the enemy of good frites
First fry at 140°C until cooked but pale, 6-7 min
Drain and cool — this is the secret of Belgian frites
Sauté shallots and celery in butter
Add mussels and wine, cover
Steam 4-5 min until all mussels open — discard any that don't
Add cream if desired, scatter parsley
Second fry potatoes at 190°C until deep golden and crispy, 2-3 min
Serve mussels in the pot, frites in a paper cone with mayonnaise — never ketchup
lunch.description: Belgium's national dish. The double-fried frites are non-negotiable, and they're served with mayonnaise — asking for ketchup marks you as a tourist.

lunch.name: Waterzooi de Poulet (Chicken Waterzooi)
instructions: Melt butter, gently sweat leeks, celery, carrots — don't brown
Add chicken pieces, broth, thyme, bay leaf
Simmer 25 min until chicken is cooked through
Add potatoes, cook 15 more min
Remove from heat
Temper egg yolks with cream, stir into broth — this enriches without boiling
Season with white pepper
Scatter with parsley
Serve in deep bowls with crusty bread
lunch.description: Ghent's famous creamy chicken stew — originally made with fish from the rivers. The egg yolk-cream liaison at the end makes it silky.

lunch.name: Stoemp (Mashed Potatoes with Vegetables)
instructions: Boil potatoes until tender
Cook chosen vegetable separately until soft
Mash potatoes with butter and cream
Fold in cooked vegetable — keep it chunky, not smooth
Season with nutmeg, salt, pepper
Serve as a bed for sausage, bratwurst, or boudin
lunch.description: Hearty mashed potato with vegetables — Brussels' everyday comfort food. Every grandmother has a favorite stoemp.

dinner.name: Carbonnade Flamande (Flemish Beef Stew)
instructions: Brown beef in batches in butter, set aside
Caramelize onions slowly in same pot, 15 min
Return beef, sprinkle flour, stir
Pour in Belgian brown ale — it must be Belgian
Add sugar, thyme, bay leaves
Spread mustard on bread slices, press them mustard-side down into the stew
Cover and simmer 2.5 hours — the bread dissolves and thickens the sauce
Add vinegar in the last 10 min — it brightens the richness
Serve with frites or boiled potatoes
dinner.description: Flemish beef braised in Belgian brown ale — the mustard-bread thickener is the traditional technique. Arguably better than French boeuf bourguignon.

dinner.name: Gentse Stoverij (Ghent-Style Beef)
instructions: Brown beef, sauté onions until deep gold
Add beer, thyme, bay leaf
Spread bread with mustard and sirop de Liège, push into stew
Simmer 2 hours until meat is fork-tender
Serve over frites
dinner.description: Ghent's variation of carbonnade — uses sirop de Liège for a sweet-sour depth unique to the city.

dinner.name: Vol-au-Vent (Chicken in Puff Pastry)
instructions: Bake vol-au-vent shells until golden and hollow
Make roux with butter and flour
Add broth gradually, whisk to smooth sauce
Poach chicken and meatballs in the sauce
Add mushrooms, cook 5 min
Stir in cream, lemon juice, nutmeg
Fill puff pastry shells
Replace pastry lids at an angle
Serve with frites — always frites
dinner.description: Puff pastry filled with chicken, meatballs, and mushrooms in creamy sauce — a Belgian brasserie classic.

snacks.name: Frites (Belgian Fries)
ingredients: Mayonnaise, andalouse, or stoofvleessaus for dipping
instructions: Cut potatoes into thick batons, at least 1cm wide — thin fries are not Belgian
Rinse in cold water, dry completely
First fry at 140°C for 6-7 min — potatoes should be cooked but still pale
Drain on wire rack, cool completely — this resting step is critical
Second fry at 190°C for 2-3 min until deep golden and crunchy outside
Shake in paper cone, salt immediately
Serve with your choice of sauce — mayonnaise is the default
snacks.description: Double-fried in beef tallow, thick-cut, served in a paper cone with mayo. Belgium invented frites — not France. The country has 5,000+ frituren (fry shops).

snacks.name: Croquettes aux Crevettes (Shrimp Croquettes)
instructions: Make thick béchamel, season with nutmeg and cayenne
Fold in shrimp and parsley — the mixture should be very thick
Spread on tray, refrigerate until completely firm (4 hours or overnight)
Shape into cylinders or ovals
Coat in flour, egg wash, fine breadcrumbs — repeat for double coating
Deep fry at 180°C for 3-4 min until deep golden
Serve immediately with lemon and fried parsley
snacks.description: Crispy outside, molten shrimp cream inside — the crown jewel of Belgian snacking. Made with tiny North Sea grey shrimp that have more flavor than their size suggests.

snacks.name: Mitraillette (Machine Gun Sandwich)
ingredients: Meat: frikandel, boulette, or viandelle (fried meat)
Sauce: andalouse, samurai, or mammoet (Belgian sauces)
instructions: Fry thick-cut frites
Split baguette
Layer: lettuce, tomato, fried meat of choice
Pile frites directly into the sandwich — generously
Drown in sauce — andalouse is the classic (tomato-mayo-pepper)
Close the baguette (it barely closes)
Eat with both hands over the wrapper — this is not elegant food
snacks.description: A baguette stuffed with fries, fried meat, and sauce — Belgium's ultimate drunk food. Named 'machine gun' for its shape. Went viral when food tourists discovered Belgium puts fries INSIDE sandwiches. Every friterie makes them.

desserts.name: Chocolate Pralines
ingredients: 500g Belgian couverture chocolate (dark, milk, or white)
Ganache filling: 200ml cream, 200g chocolate, flavorings (coffee, hazelnut, raspberry, caramel)
instructions: Temper chocolate: melt to 55°C, cool to 27°C, reheat to 31°C — this gives the signature snap
Polish molds, coat with thin layer of tempered chocolate, let set
Make ganache: heat cream, pour over chopped chocolate, stir until smooth
Add flavoring of choice, cool until pipeable
Pipe ganache into chocolate shells
Seal with another layer of tempered chocolate
Unmold once fully set — they should release with a gentle tap
Store at 15-18°C — never in the fridge
desserts.description: Belgium's most famous export after beer. Belgian pralines were invented in 1912 by Jean Neuhaus in Brussels. The country has over 2,000 chocolate shops.

desserts.name: Tarte au Riz (Rice Tart)
ingredients: Filling: 150g pudding rice, 1L milk, 3 eggs, 150g sugar, vanilla, lemon zest, nutmeg
instructions: Blind-bake pastry shell
Simmer rice in milk until tender and creamy, 30 min
Cool slightly, beat in eggs, sugar, vanilla, lemon zest, nutmeg
Pour into pastry shell
Bake at 160°C for 40-45 min until set with golden spots on top
Cool to room temperature — it firms as it cools
desserts.description: Liège's beloved rice custard tart — found in every boulangerie in Wallonia. Creamy, eggy, and comforting.

drinks.name: Belgian Trappist Beer
ingredients: One Trappist beer: Chimay, Orval, Westmalle, Rochefort, Westvleteren, or Achel
instructions: Pour slowly into the correct branded glass — each abbey has its own
Tilt glass at 45°, pour steadily
Leave the yeast sediment in the bottle (or pour it in if you prefer)
Serve at 8-12°C, not fridge-cold
Savor — these beers are brewed by monks in six recognized Belgian abbeys
drinks.description: Belgium has 6 of the world's 14 Trappist breweries. Westvleteren 12 is regularly voted the world's best beer. Each is brewed by Cistercian monks.

drinks.name: Jenever (Belgian Gin)
ingredients: Jenever (Belgian grain spirit, old-style or young-style)
instructions: Pour jenever into small tulip glass, filled to the brim
The first sip is taken by bending down to the glass on the bar — no hands — called a kopstoot
Then lift and sip normally
Traditionally accompanied by beer as a 'kopstoot' (headbutt) pairing
drinks.description: Belgium's native spirit — older than gin, distilled from malted grain. The hands-free first sip from a brimming glass is a sacred pub ritual.

drinks.name: Chocolat Chaud (Belgian Hot Chocolate)
instructions: Heat milk and cream until steaming
Add chopped chocolate, whisk until fully melted and smooth
Simmer gently 2 min — it should be thick and glossy
Pour into mugs
Top with whipped cream and chocolate shavings
drinks.description: Made with real melted Belgian chocolate — thick enough to coat a spoon. A world apart from powdered cocoa.
